heroSummary: The Bambu Lab A1 achieves reliable print speeds up to 190 mm/s capped at a 16 mm³/s maximum volumetric flow rate with Overture Rock PLA. However, because this mineral-filled composite is abrasive, upgrading from the stock stainless steel nozzle to a Bambu hardened steel hotend assembly is mandatory to prevent rapid bore wear.
bedSurfaceRecommendation: Bambu Textured PEI Plate without glue (clean thoroughly with dish soap and warm water)
slicerTweaks: Set 'Max volumetric speed' in Filament Settings to 16 mm³/s to prevent underextrusion at high traversal speeds.
Configure Nozzle Temperature to 208°C and Bed Temperature to 55°C for optimal interlayer bonding and consistent matte sheen.
Set Pressure Advance (PA) to approximately 0.026 via manual calibration to eliminate corner bulging caused by mineral particulate drag.
Switch Wall Order to 'Inner/Outer' and constrain outer wall speed to 100 mm/s to ensure a uniform faux-stone exterior finish.

troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Abrasive stone/mineral composite particles rapidly cutting into the stock stainless steel nozzle tip.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Upgrade the toolhead to the Bambu Lab 0.4mm or 0.6mm Hardened Steel Hotend assembly.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: First layer warping or corner lifting
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Oils on the textured PEI surface or bed temperature set below the polymer transition point.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Scrub the PEI sheet with dish soap and warm water, avoid skin contact, and raise first layer bed temperature to 60°C.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Brittle structural strength / weak layer adhesion
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Excessive part cooling fan speeds chilling the mineral-filled polymer before proper molecular cross-bonding occurs.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Lower minimum cooling fan speed to 60% and raise print temperature to 215°C for functional mechanical prints.

faq.question: Can I run Overture Rock PLA through the stock Bambu A1 stainless steel nozzle?
faq.answer: You can for a few small prints, but the mineral additives will erode stainless steel quickly, altering the nozzle orifice diameter and destroying print precision. Always upgrade to a hardened steel hotend.

faq.question: Is Overture Rock PLA compatible with the Bambu AMS Lite?
faq.answer: Yes, Overture plastic spools rotate cleanly on the AMS Lite rotary holders, and the filament feeds smoothly through the PTFE tubing without snagging.

faq.question: Why does the surface gloss look uneven across my printed model?
faq.answer: Variations in print speed cause temperature differences that alter the matte dispersion; clamp inner and outer wall speeds to identical values to maintain a uniform matte texture.

faq.question: Does Overture Rock PLA require active filament drying before printing?
faq.answer: Standard PLA is not strongly hygroscopic, but mineral additives can trap surface moisture over time; if popping occurs or stringing increases, dry at 45°C to 50°C for 6 hours.
